purpose: Reviewable primary-source data for water-charge comparisons and read-only public request status. Not a determination of overcharging or proof that a repair was completed.

water_rates.effective_date_source_section: Utility Rate Resolution; also Schedule 7, Water
water_rates.effective_basis: Meter read date, not the date the user pays the bill.
water_rates.scope_end_note: Conservative implementation cutoff for this researched 2026 schedule; not a claim the ordinance automatically expires then. Re-verify any 2027 bill.
water_rates.supported_scope: Monthly in-city residential retail water, standard meter, known billed usage and meter-read date. Water charges only.

separate_safe_drinking_water_fee.handling: Show separately. Do not infer a missing monthly cent or bill adjustment from the rounded annual/monthly difference.

calculation_rules: Read actual billed water usage in CCF and multiply by 3.88; compare only the water usage line.
If usage is in cubic feet, divide by 100. Prefer billed CCF to conversion from gallons because 748 is approximate.
Compare the meter-size fixed WATER line separately. Never use the SEWER fixed charge table.
The resolution applies the monthly fixed fee to each billing period or partial period. Do not invent day-proration rules.
Do not apply sewer average-winter-consumption rules to water usage.
Use decimal currency arithmetic, show rounding and label a mismatch as a question to ask the utility. Supplier rounding of fractional usage was not verified.
water_rates.source_note: The official rates page was last updated July 23, 2026. The adopted budget confirms rates for meter reads on/after January 1, 2026. The outside-city sewer figure $38.90 is a monthly sewer-only fee, NOT a per-CCF water rate.

water_rates.supported_scope: Monthly single-family treated-water account with service class, meter size and provider's winter threshold confirmed. Water only; exclude unusual billing periods.

tier_thresholds.tier1_end_gallons: T = clamp(average January-February-March billed monthly gallons, 5000, 15000)
tier_thresholds.winter_threshold_note: Prefer the account's provider-confirmed AWC/tier1 threshold. Never assume every home gets the same threshold.

drought.handling: Apply to confirmed May2026-or-later usage within the researched 2026 schedule. For boundary/straddling bills ask the utility; do not infer from bill date alone. Re-verify base2027 rates even though drought pricing may continue.

calculation_rules: For monthly gallons G and confirmed threshold T: V1=min(G,T), V2=min(max(G-T,0),15000), V3=max(G-T-15000,0).
Base usage charge=sum(Vi/1000 * applicable base rate i). Drought charge=sum(Vi/1000 * surcharge i), when applicable. Add the separate fixed water charge only for the matched meter size.
Require the customer class from the bill; city-name text alone cannot distinguish inside-city, read-and-bill and total-service classes.
Compare water usage, drought and fixed lines separately. Do not declare the entire bill incorrect.

recommended.type: Public CKAN datastore read API; not an Open311 submission API
recommended.filter_semantics: Exact JSON filter on the published 311 case number. Preserve punctuation and leading zeros. unique_id adds creation year; do not assume case_number alone is globally unique.
parser_rules: Check success=true, then read result.records; no records means not found in this public feed, not an invalid request.
Keep status text exactly, including any Duplicate flag. Known values include New, Open, Closed and In Progress; preserve unfamiliar values.
If multiple rows share a case number, ask the user to select the matching year/subject; retain unique_id.
UTC-named fields are UTC even when serialized without a trailing Z. Use these rather than assuming Eastern timestamps are UTC.
Closed means the agency closed its case. It does not prove the underlying repair was completed or the water is safe.
Select only the allowlisted fields. No address/location or reporter data is needed for a case-number lookup.
recommended.published_refresh: Four publications daily around 02:17, 08:17, 14:17, 20:17 local time; not a real-time connection to agency staff.
recommended.coverage: Pittsburgh municipal311 records from new system introduced2025-02-04 plus imported legacy records back to2015. Not every water utility work order or private landlord request is a municipal311 case.
limits: Privacy rules restrict some request/location data.
The separate old archive stopped updating2025-02-04; do not use resource29462525-62a6-45bf-9b5e-ad2e1c06348d for current tracking.
Network failures must show unavailable, not closed or not found.
Credit City of Pittsburgh / WPRDC and link the source; dataset is Creative Commons Attribution.

observed_duplicate_example.note: Exact lookup returned different requests from2016 and2024; ask for matching year.

nyc_receipt_lookup_not_supported.reason: Official dictionary states unique_key is NOT the Service Request number given to the initiating customer; SR numbers are absent. Do not use a receipt number as unique_key or infer a mapping.
nyc_receipt_lookup_not_supported.refresh: Overnight with a one-day buffer, per official dictionary.
